increment_paragraph: **CURRENT-CONTEXT-NEW-TRIAGE, D3** (USER DECISION 2026-11-16, D1/D3 "Queue both (Recommended)"; gateway rule 11v (5), contract specification §C04.6.1, qcore-schemas 27.0.0 `ResourceKind::ThreadKey`; Lean `QCore.ThreadKeyStatic`; [report](../../reports/current-context-new-triage/README.md)). `pthread_key_create` and `pthread_key_delete` are declared in `quirin-provider-libc` with the second in-place kind, `thread_key`, finalised by value; the creation applies only with a null destructor (C04.5), and §C04.5.1 now admits the C11 6.3.2.3p3 null pointer constant `(void *) 0` (glibc's `NULL`) at a pointer premise of `0`, structurally (USER DECISION 2026-11-16, "Admit (void *) 0 (Recommended)"; Lean `QCore.NullPointerConstantPremise`); scalar premises are unchanged. A key created into anything but static storage refuses (an automatic key would be tracked by value, and the gate found a statement fallback that re-lowered `(void) pthread_getspecific(k)` as a plain borrowed call); a key created into `&G` of an unshadowed static-duration object (not thread-local) binds no frame obligation and needs no status witness, held by static storage under the stated premise P-THREAD-KEY-STATIC. A static key's delete, a key reached through a pointer, a thread-local key and an untracked delete refuse. Predicted: `mk_http_thread_initialize_tls_once` `Unknown -> Safe` (corpus and the user's current); system and slice unchanged; `mk_plugin_preworker_calls` stays Unknown (its key is reached through `node->thread_key`).

ledger.text: Narrowed by CURRENT-CONTEXT-NEW-TRIAGE (D3, gateway rule 11v (5)): the pthread_key_create/pthread_key_delete pair is declared with the in-place kind thread_key (finalised by value, null destructor only); a key created into a static-duration object is held by the static owner under the stated premise P-THREAD-KEY-STATIC, and an automatic key is CG25's protocol. Still open for this pair: a key reached through a pointer (mk_plugin_preworker_calls, mk_fifo_create), a key with a destructor (a registration), and a static key's delete (mk_tls_exit), each refused. The other pairs are unchanged.

ledger.title: C1: keyed-slot retention for internal-linkage pthread keys, with a unit-level slot-protocol pass
ledger.text: Read pthread_getspecific(k) as "NULL or an object one of the unit's pthread_setspecific(k, .) sites stored on this thread" only for a key of internal linkage whose every pthread_key_create/setspecific/getspecific/delete site is in the unit (Monkey's local_context in lib/monkey/tls/tls_openssl.c); an external-linkage key, a key reached through a pointer and any __thread object refuse; a reader must test NULL (get before set is NULL). Needs a unit-level pass before per-function analysis and a libc keyed retention clause (C04.14 extended) in quirin-provider-libc threads.qv. Depends on D3 (thread_key kind). PREDICTION-C share: with C2 makes mk_tls_thread_init Safe; with C4/C5 makes context_get_head, tls_event_interest, context_get Safe (current only). DISCHARGE: the clause, the pass, Lean parity, fixtures (external key refused, get-before-set NULL guard required), measured on the user's current. USER DECISION 2026-11-16 (verbatim): context_new -> "C: derived -> Safe"; the integrator split C into these layers. Correction recorded with D3: mk_plugin_preworker_calls stays Unknown (its key is reached through node->thread_key), unlike PROPOSAL.md's D3 row. ledger.title: A statement fallback can re-lower a cast-to-void call over a tracked in-place object as a plain borrowed call
ledger.text: CURRENT-CONTEXT-NEW-TRIAGE (D3) measured (private/repro/probe-getter.log): with a tracked automatic thread key, `(void) pthread_getspecific(key)` was admitted Safe even after `pthread_key_delete(key)`, while `pthread_getspecific(key);` and `v = pthread_getspecific(key);` were refused by rule 11v (4)'s guard. The cast statement's first classification is an older refusal, which the guard skips, and a later statement fallback (the cast route's uncast lowering) re-lowers the uncast call without the guard. D3 avoids it by never tracking a thread key. The same shape over a tracked regex object (`(void) f(&re, …)` at an unkinded position) is not measured. A guard widened to every refusal mentioning a tracked object broke rd_regex_match's admitted `r = k_regexec(&re, str) != 1;`, and a CFG-level name check misses a by-value scalar actual (no place is recorded). DISCHARGE: apply rule 11v (4)'s guard to every fallback's admitted lowering (or carry the actual's name for by-value scalars into the node), with a fixture per kind, and measure.
